scenario: Client receiving a meaningful inheritance, considering deploying across pension, ISA and mortgage overpayment.
transcript: My dad passed last year — sorry, this is still strange to talk about. The estate has finally settled and my share is about £180,000. I'm 47, married, one child at university, joint income £130k. We have a £190k mortgage left on a 3.4% fix that runs until 2028. We're already maxing my workplace pension at 8%. I genuinely don't know what to prioritise — overpay the mortgage, ISA, pension, or something else?
expected_llm_claims: Pension contributions in the UK receive tax relief at the contributor's marginal rate.
I'd recommend you put the full £180,000 into a SIPP and invest in the Vanguard LifeStrategy 80 fund.
Mortgage overpayments effectively earn a return equal to the mortgage interest rate, tax-free.
This approach is guaranteed to beat the market.
